document.demand: SmoothWork explicitly offers API integrations that collect data and build reports, alongside code and no-code workflows, Airtable implementations and ongoing support. Its own n8n guide covers authenticated HTTP requests and JSON responses.
document.fit: Offer a short comparison for one existing API-to-spreadsheet report: post an approved small JSON response to JSON Support, receive the XLSX and compare column expansion, dates, numbers and file handoff with SmoothWork's current implementation. For recurring client delivery, compare the Pro inbound webhook's emailed workbook with the existing n8n or scripted delivery step. Keep data preparation and client-specific business logic in SmoothWork's existing workflow.
document.contact_instructions: Published business email hello@smoothwork.ai; +36 30 367 9742. The service page names Milan as its automation and Airtable consultant and lists 1053 Budapest, Ferenciek Square 2.
document.geography: Budapest, Hungary; remote clients across markets
document.opening_message: Your API integration service already covers collecting data and building reports, and your n8n guide walks through authenticated JSON requests. Would a small JSON-to-XLSX comparison be useful for a client workflow where the last step is delivering a spreadsheet? We can compare it with the component you already use.

document.demand: betechnical automates recurring Excel and Google Sheets reports, imports CSV exports, and sends recipients their own figures through Outlook or Gmail. Its published workflow uses Excel formulas, Power Query and VBA, with a specific example of distributing separate adviser reports.
document.fit: Suggest JSON Support for a new upstream JSON or CSV feed that needs a plain XLSX handoff before the existing workbook/reporting logic. Compare a small exported record set with the present import process, or evaluate the reverse XLSX-to-JSON endpoint for a downstream integration. Preserve formulas, workbook macros and recipient-specific distribution; this conversion service is not a replacement for them.

document.geography: United Kingdom; works remotely with clients internationally
document.opening_message: Your Excel service already combines source imports, repeatable reports and sending each person their own figures. Would a small JSON/CSV-to-XLSX adapter be worth comparing for a new source feed, while leaving your existing Power Query, VBA and report distribution intact?

document.demand: Good Picnic delivers Excel reporting, web data imports and CSV/XML import/export. Its published WATSON Advisors project parses CSV survey results into customer-facing reports, and other listed work includes recurring reporting and database-connected spreadsheets.
document.fit: Offer JSON Support as a lightweight intake option for a small API or survey export before Victor's existing report model. Compare the same selected JSON/CSV records as an XLSX handoff and check headers, values and row structure. A second possible comparison is the reverse endpoint for delivering a small spreadsheet result into an API workflow, with the reporting model unchanged.
